question.text: When two compounds ACl<sub>3</sub> and DCl<sub>3</sub> of two elements A and D are mixed together a compound ADCl<sub>6</sub> is formed. Structural analysis showed that ADCl<sub>6</sub> is an ionic compound. Given that DCl<sub>3</sub> is trigonal planar and ACl<sub>3</sub> is trigonal pyramidal, predict the shape of the anion <math> <mrow> <msubsup> <mtext>DCl</mtext> <mn>4</mn> <mo>-</mo> </msubsup> </mrow> </math>.

solution.text:
⇒ As DCl3 is trigonal planar, hence, 'D' belongs to boron family.

⇒ As ACl3 is trigonal pyramidal, hence, 'A' belongs to nitrogen family.

⇒ DCl3 + ACl3 → [DCl2]+ [ACl4]–

or  [ACl2]+ [DCl4]–

if anionic part is [ACl4]– which has See - saw structure then cationic part will be [DCl2]+ where hybridization of D will be 'sp' and hence, shape will be linear.

⇒  If anionic part is DCl 4 - i.e, it is of tetrahedral shape the cation part will be ACl 2 + which will be bent with sp2 hybridisation.
